Everything You Need to Know About the Gates Cambridge Scholarship
description: Have you ever thought about studying abroad for graduate school? Then check out the Gates Cambridge Scholarship, which allows students to get their masters or PhD from one of the most reputable universities in the UK free of cost! This scholarship is highly valuable, covering the full cost of tuition, an allowance for living expenses, visa and health insurance and much more. Keep reading to learn more about the Gates Cambridge Scholarship and tips about how to win it! Also see: Top graduate school scholarships At a glance The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is an opportunity for students outside of the UK to earn their postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge free of cost. Students are considered for the scholarship automatically when they apply to Cambridge. There are only 80 awards available each year, making this a very competitive and prestigious scholarship. What is the Gates Cambridge Scholarship? The Gates Cambridge Scholarship gives students outside of the UK the opportunity to study and earn their masters or PhD at the prestigious University of Cambridge. Each year, the Gates Cambridge Trust awards this scholarship to 80 high-achieving students to pursue a postgraduate degree. Keep in mind about two-thirds of the awards go to PhD students, and approximately 25 awards are available to students from the US and 55 available to other International students outside of the US and UK. This makes the scholarship highly competitive, but for good reason, as it offers many benefits. Core awards for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship Each scholarship covers the full cost of studying at Cambridge, plus some additional funding: The University Composition Fee at the appropriate rate (this fee varies depending on the student) A maintenance allowance for a single student (£21,000 for 12 months at the 2024-25 rate; pro rata for courses shorter than 12 months) – for PhD scholars the award is for up to 4 years One economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course Inbound visa costs & the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge Circumstantial additional funding The trust may also award additional funding to applicants with certain circumstances. Applications are viewed on a discretionary basis. These discretionary components include: Academic development funding – from up to £500 to up to £2,000, dependent on the length of your course, to attend conferences and courses. Dependent Children Allowance – up to £11,604 for one child and up to £16,548 for two or more children (2024-25 rate). No funding is provided for a partner. Fieldwork – you may apply to retain your normal maintenance allowance while on fieldwork as part of your PhD (the Trust does not fund other fieldwork costs as these should be funded by the University Composition Fee). Maternity/Paternity funding – should you require it, you may apply to intermit your studies for up to 6 months and continue to receive your maintenance allowance during this time Hardship funding – for unforeseen difficulties facing the scholar Who’s eligible to apply for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship? In order to apply for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship, students must be: A citizen of any country outside the United Kingdom Applying to pursue one of the following courses at the University of Cambridge: PhD (full-time or part-time*) MLitt (full-time) One year postgraduate course (full-time), with some exceptions Students who applied for October 2024 entry are eligible for a pilot program at Cambridge which allows funding for part-time PhD students. As for the selection criteria , Cambridge uses four key criteria to select their scholarship winners: academic excellence, reasons for choice of course, a commitment to improving the lives of others, and a capacity of leadership. How to apply for the Cambridge Gates Scholarship The Gates Cambridge Scholarship has a combined admissions form with Cambridge University’s graduate school application. This means that when students apply for a graduate program through Cambridge’s graduate application portal , Cambridge automatically considers them for the Gates Cambridge scholarship along with additional funding. For the overall application you’ll need to provide details about your academic background, your future plans, and why you’re suitable for the course you want to study. You’ll also need to gather the following materials: References Transcripts CV/resume English language test results (if English is not your first language) Personal statement Written work (only certain courses) Graduate Record Examination (GRE) test score (only for some departments) Financial documents PhD applicants must also submit a research proposal to qualify for funding. Then you’ll move on to the Gates Cambridge sub-section. Gates Cambridge statement The Gates Cambridge statement is an approximately 500 word (3000 characters) essay where you’ll explain why you’re applying for the scholarship and how you meet the four main criteria (academic excellence, reasons for choice of course, a commitment to improving the lives of others, and a capacity of leadership.) This is the only part of the application where they specifically ask you about why you are a good fit for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship. Use this space to distinguish yourself from other candidates by drawing on past experiences and achievements and future goals and connecting them directly with the scholarship. Gates Cambridge references In addition to two references for admission into Cambridge, Gate Cambridge applicants must submit an additional reference specific to the scholarship. That means you’ll need 3 total references to apply. Cambridge asks referees to rank applicants and rate how well suited they are for the scholarship based on how well they follow the four criteria mentioned above on a scale of exceptional, strong, not strong, and weak. Keep in mind that you should avoid having friends or family members write your references. Instead, Cambridge recommends individuals like current or former academic advisors who are aware of your personal attributes, a current or former employer, or a senior member of an organisation with whom you have volunteered. Final Interviews Once you have been accepted to a department/course, Cambridge’s academic departments will review your application and nominate a small number of eligible applicants to go forward in the process. Nominated applicants are invited to do a short interview to see if they align with the four main criteria. The interview can be either virtual or in person depending on your location and lasts between 25 and 30 minutes. You’ll be interviewing with a panel of experienced academics and practitioners and potentially with Cambridge alumni and representatives of the Gates Cambridge Trust. The interview is structured in 4 main sections: Introduction (The panel will be introduced to you and tell you about the format of the interview and any other essential information for a productive conversation.) Gates Cambridge (You’ll be asked about what you know about the Gates Cambridge scholarship, your motivations to apply, why you think you’d be a good scholar, and your thoughts on the opportunity.) Academic and career plans (A space to talk about your past experience, your course at Cambridge, and what you plan to do with your career.) Final thoughts and questions (An opportunity to convey any additional questions or information for the panel.) Scholarship application timeline The application cycle for 2026-2027 opens in early September of 2025. The official dates for 2026-2027 have not yet been released, but here is last year’s cycle timeline for reference: Applications open: Wednesday, September 4th, 2024 Application deadline: Wednesday, October 16, 2024 All applicants notified of application outcome: Wednesday, December 11, 2024 Review and selection by panels: Friday, January 24th, and Saturday January 25th, 2025 Scholarships offered: Monday, February 3, 2025 Tips on winning the Gates Cambridge scholarships Applying to the Gates Cambridge Scholarship requires you to first gather all the materials needed to apply to Cambridge. Your first step is to make sure you have all the required materials ready and at their best, like getting optimal scores on the GRE and updating your resume . As for the Gates Cambridge specific areas of the application, this is where you can really shine and set yourself apart from other candidates. Gates Cambridge Statement 500 words is not very much when it comes to a personal statement, so try to be concise and impactful. Start planning your essay by listing out different experiences and achievements that connect directly to Gates Cambridge’s four main criteria (intellectual ability, justification for the choice of course, a commitment to improving the lives of others and leadership capacity.) Then select the ones you feel most confident writing about. If you want some more tips on how to write a 500 word essay, check out our writing guide ! Along with your statement, your references are a big part of your application that will help you stand out from the competition. It’s important to be strategic when it comes to picking who your references will be. As mentioned earlier, steer clear of friends and family and focus on mentors, advisors/instructors, and employers. Make sure to give them plenty of time to complete your references. Asking for a letter of recommendation last minute usually doesn’t yield the best results. Keep reading : How to write a graduate school personal statement (with examples!) Finalist Interviews If you are invited to interview, congratulations! This means you’ve made it to the finalist round. The interview is still very important, as it is your final chance to impress the committee before they decide on scholarship winners. To prepare, check out the Gates Cambridge selection page where they break down the interview process and point out some potential questions and talking points. When preparing for the interview, practice is your best tool. Whether you are practicing with friends or family, or just in front of the mirror, this can help build your confidence. But remember, Gates Cambridge is looking for this to be a conversation, so while memorizing talking points and having an idea of what you want to say is great, don’t write out your answers and rehearse them like a speech. Reciting rehearsed answers can come off a bit stiff and robotic. Overall, do your best to stay relaxed, confident, and ready to answer any question that comes your way. See also: 15 scholarship interview questions (and how to respond!) Additional resources If you have more questions about the Gates Cambridge Scholarship, we encourage you to head to their website . They have lots of information regarding how to apply, how they select winners, and past scholar profiles. And keep in mind that while this opportunity is awesome, many other excellent scholarships and grants are available for postgraduate students planning to study abroad. For example: The Boren Awards Fulbright Global Scholar Award To learn more about other postgraduate scholarship opportunities , make a free Scholarships360 account to get matched to vetted scholarships based on your preferences. Good luck on your scholarship search! Start your scholarship search Vetted scholarships custom-matched to your profile Access exclusive scholarships only available to Scholarships360 members Get Started Key Takeaways The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a great opportunity for students outside interested in studying at the University of Cambridge. To apply, students have to select and be accepted to a specific course/department at Cambridge. Then, they are automatically considered for the scholarship. Scholarship finalists must do a short interview with academic experts and members of the Gates Cambridge Trust in order to win. Frequently asked questions about the Gates Cambridge Scholarship How competitive is the Gates Cambridge Scholarship? The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is extremely competitive with only 80 scholars chosen a year. Only a very small percentage of applicants actually win the scholarship. Winners of this scholarship typically have outstanding academics (with a GPA of 3.8 or higher), have shown a commitment to improving the lives of others, have evidence of leadership potential, and demonstrate to Cambridge that they are a clear fit with the university. Is there an interview for the Gates Cambridge Scholarship? Yes, there is an interview for finalists of the Gates Cambridge scholarship. A small number of applicants are chosen to move forward based on nominations from their chosen academic department. The interview is about 25-30 minutes long with a panel of academic experts and members of the Gates Cambridge Trust. How much is the Gates Cambridge stipend? The stipend for living expenses for the Gates Cambridge scholarship is £21,000 for 12 months. If your program is shorter than 12 months, the rate will be adjusted proportionately. The stipend is renewable for up to 4 years for PhD students.

title: How to Win Local Scholarships
description: Why you should apply to local scholarships Although big-name scholarships tend to get the most coverage, local scholarships are actually a better fit for the majority of students. Every student who enters a local scholarship competition has a better chance of winning than those who throw their name into the bigger competitions. Even winners of national scholarships agree. We spoke to Sophia Weber, who won the Coca-Cola Scholars program, about her scholarship strategy. She said “I think the biggest thing is not focusing only on how much a scholarship is worth. Every little bit helps—$50, $100, it all adds up. At first, I was only going after full rides and big national scholarships, but once I started applying for smaller and local ones too, I realized how much they really made a difference.” Local scholarships allow you to apply to niche scholarships that fit your background and interests. Make sure to include them in your scholarship strategy along with the big-name opportunities. Where to find local scholarships To win local scholarships, your first step should be knowing where to look. Here are some of the best places to find local scholarships: Start with your school The best place to start when looking for local scholarships is always your school. If you are a college-bound high school student, be sure to check-in with both your high school’s college counselor and the financial aid department at your future college. Financial aid professionals and college counselors make it their job to send students to college and find financially viable routes for them to pay tuition. So, these people will have an extensive knowledge of the scholarships available for local students. Oftentimes, they will be able to offer you a list of the best local scholarship opportunities to consider. In addition to speaking directly with counselors, you can check the website of both your high school and your college. Oftentimes, they maintain a page of scholarships in the community that offers some great options. And remember – you can qualify for local scholarships in the community you’re from and in the community you’re planning on attending college. Research past scholarships that students at your high school have received Every year, high schools around the country put together a list of graduates for the commencement program. Sometimes these programs include information such as where the students are attending college or which students won certain awards or scholarships. This was the case at the high school I worked at as a guidance counselor. The list of awards and scholarships is a fantastic shortcut for finding all of the scholarships that the previous high school class won. If you can get a copy of the program (some of these programs may even be online), you will have a great list of scholarships that you may apply for. Expert Perspective I think of scholarships in three categories: national, niche, and local. National Scholarships: These are well-known opportunities often highlighted on trusted resources like Scholarships360. Niche Scholarships: These might be based on unique traits, talents, or affiliations (e.g., being left-handed or part of a particular community group). Local Scholarships: Don’t overlook these! Many smaller, local scholarships receive few applications, so the odds can be in your favor. Even if the award is small, it’s worth applying. For example, would you spend an hour writing an essay for $300? Most people would! Finally, familiarize yourself with funding options at the colleges you’re applying to. Some schools meet 100% of demonstrated need, limit loans, or automatically consider applicants for merit aid. Always shoot your shot and apply for opportunities—it’s worth the time and effort. Sara Elaine Hart | Director of the Walentas Scholars Program , Former High School Counselor Check the organizations you’re already involved in Once you’ve checked in with your current and/or future school, it’s time to ask around at the local organizations you’re involved with. Whether that is a place of worship, an athletic club, a volunteer organization, a hobby group, the Scouts, or any other structured activity you’re a part of, they might offer scholarships for their members. Even if they don’t offer a scholarship themselves, they may know of opportunities in the community. Be sure to ask a member of your organization who is well-connected in the community – the more deeply rooted they are, the better chance there is that they will know of local opportunities you may qualify for. Check community organizations Most community organizations keep a list of local scholarships, and some even offer their own. If you’re not sure about the nearest community organization to you, try the Council on Foundations’ Community Foundation Locator . Apply to these exclusive scholarships See all opportunities $10,000 "No Essay" Scholarship 1 award worth $10,000 Open to All Grade Levels Apply "College Here I Come" Essay Scholarship for High School Seniors 1 award worth $1,000 Open to High School Senior Apply "Broad Horizons" Scholarship for High School Juniors 1 award worth $1,000 Open to High School Junior Apply "Making Waves" Scholarship for Women 1 award worth $1,000 Open to All Grade Levels Apply "Tuition Solution" Scholarship for STEM Students 1 award worth $1,000 Open to All Grade Levels Apply "A Helping Hand" Scholarship 1 award worth $1,000 Open to High School Seniors, College & Graduate Students Apply See all opportunities Find local chapters of national organizations There are many national organizations out there that run local chapters across the country. Here are a couple examples of national organizations that run regional chapters that often offer scholarships: Elks Club The Benevolent and Protective Order of Elks is a national organization focused on philanthropy, patriotism, and other similar initiatives. They have chapters all across the country, and many of these chapters offer scholarships to students in their area. Some scholarship opportunities are only for Elks Club members and children of Elks Club members, while others are open to the general population. Scouts Scouts organizations, such as the Boy Scouts of America , and Girl Scouts of America , are another national organization with chapters all across the country. They offer national scholarships, as well as regional and local scholarship opportunities. Some of these opportunities are only open to members of the organization, whereas others are open to the public. If you are a current member of the Scouts, try looking for scholarships specifically for Eagle Scouts . Rotary Club The Rotary Club is a global organization that began in Chicago in 1905. They have regional chapters all over the United States. It is a service organization that works to better each community it is part of. One of their main initiatives, started in 1985, was to vaccinate all the world’s children against polio. Be sure to check out your local chapter of the Rotary Club for scholarship opportunities that fit your profile. You’ll be especially eligible for these scholarships if you are involved in community service projects . Lions Club Lions Club International is another global service organization that helps mobilize its members to do good for their community. Check with your local chapter to see if they offer scholarships to the community! VFW The Veterans of Foreign Wars organization has chapters across the country, and they offer scholarships on both a national level and a local level, depending on where you live. Even if you don’t have veterans in your family, it’s worth checking to see if your local chapter offers scholarships. Some of their opportunities are open to the public, such as the Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest . Related: Top scholarships for veterans and the children of veterans 4-H Club 4-H is another national organization that focuses on the development of America’s youth. They are especially popular in agricultural communities, and they give many children the opportunity to care for and raise an animal. Be sure to check in with your local chapter to see what funds they may offer, and whether you qualify for them! Check local businesses Many local businesses also offer scholarships to students in their community. Businesses like law firms and local banks may offer funds to college-bound students. Your college counselor will typically be well-informed about these opportunities, so be sure to check in with them. Related: How to win corporate scholarships Look for programs with your employers or your parents’ employers Tuition reimbursement is an increasingly popular benefit that employers offer their employees. But not everyone knows about it, and many people are unaware that some tuition reimbursement programs can benefit their children and family members. If you are currently employed, check in with your HR department to see if these programs are available. And if you are a high school student who thinks you won’t qualify because your job is not in your intended career, think again! Employers like Chipotle and McDonald’s offer tuition reimbursement programs to employees such as cooks and cashiers, even if their field of study is unrelated to the service industry. You should also encourage your parents to check-in with their jobs. Some tuition reimbursement programs extend these benefits to the children of employees. Related: Top 15 companies that offer tuition reimbursement Research professional organizations If you are already enrolled in college and/or have a strong idea of the career path you hope to pursue, try looking up some professional organizations that are relevant to your field. Many offer scholarships to students pursuing a relevant degree, such as the American Psychological Association’s scholarships . However, many of these opportunities require you to be a member to apply. This typically comes with a monthly or annual fee, though they are typically discounted for students. Check for government grants Students from all across the country qualify for federal grants such as the Pell Grant or the TEACH Grant . But did you know that many local governments also offer scholarships and grants to students in their community? The best way to find out about these is by reaching out to your high school’s college counselor, as well as your college’s financial aid and admissions offices. Search scholarships by state To get you started on local scholarships, try finding your state on our list of scholarships by state . These vetted opportunities are localized to each individual state, so you won’t have as much competition as you will in national scholarships. How to win local scholarships Winning scholarships is an art, and if you’re in the application process, you’ll probably write a lot of essays and personal statements. Like any scholarship, local scholarships require strong essays and applications to win. However, there is a specific art to putting together a winning local scholarship application. Local organizations are looking for students who are community-minded. Here are some tips to fine-tune your application to appeal to the organizations that will be reading your essays. Discuss how you hope to use your degree to give back to your community Local scholarships exist to improve their communities by educating the youth. They want to know that you plan to use your degree to make a difference in your community and continue to pay it forward. So, in your applications, try discussing the aspects of your community that contributed to your growth and how you hope to build on them to help future generations. If your community is facing any specific issues, you can write about how these issues motivate you and how you hope to remedy them in the future. Related: How to write an essay about yourself Reflect on how your community has shaped you In your essays and personal statements , discuss how your ambitions, strengths, and passions were shaped by your community. Try to emphasize what you’ve gained from growing up as part of your community, and then talk about how you hope to use these skills to make a difference in the world. Brainstorm a list of ways you’ve participated in your community When it comes to scholarship essays, it’s important to show, rather than tell . Don’t just say how much you care for your community – describe the ways you’ve participated and then build on them to illustrate what you hope to do in the future. Remember, participation doesn’t always have to be formal roles that you’ve held. If you shovel your neighbor’s driveway in the winter, or play pickup basketball at the park, these are all forms of participation in your community. If you describe what these activities mean to you, they can be powerful additions to a scholarship application. Talk to local leaders One great way to put together strong local scholarship applications is to talk to local leaders. Anyone who is deeply involved in your community could be a good candidate. Tell them the scholarship you’re applying for and ask for pointers on what to focus on in your application. Oftentimes, these community leaders will be more than happy to help and offer great advice. Consider in-state tuition at a public university One of the best ways to bring down the cost of college by keeping it local is by applying to an in-state public university. Public universities offer steep tuition discounts to in-state students. Oftentimes, this discount can exceed 50%. On top of that, many schools reserve select academic and merit scholarships for students who are from their state. To give you an idea of how substantial this tuition discount can be, we can look at the 2025-2026 tuition rates at Miami University in Ohio. Tuition for non-Ohio residents is $38,682 per year, whereas in-state students pay $15,161 in tuition. This is over a 50% discount. Also, remember that it’s possible to get in-state tuition as an out-of-state student ! Many states have struck up reciprocity agreements , meaning that students from both states can receive tuition discounts at public universities in either state. One of the biggest examples of these agreements is the Western Undergraduate Exchange . This agreement provides tuition discounts to students in sixteen states. Staying up to date on opportunities in your area Once you go out into your community and ask your high school counselor, your future college’s financial aid office, and your community leaders, you should have a good lay of the land as far as local scholarships go. But what if new opportunities open up in the future? How can you stay on top of local scholarships while still putting your all into schoolwork, extracurriculars , and your other responsibilities? Luckily, we can lend you a hand. Our free scholarship matching tool updates every day with new scholarship opportunities matched specifically to your profile. It only takes a couple minutes to sign up, and once you have an account, you can login anytime to see an updated list of scholarships matched specifically to you. Expert Perspective Some high schools keep their own scholarship database, which can be a great way for students to keep track of scholarships in their area and when they are due. Melody Lipford | Advising Specialist on the Virtual Access Team, College Possible Advantages and disadvantages of local scholarships Now that you’ve got the rundown on how to find and apply for local scholarships, let’s get into some of their advantages and disadvantages. This will help you decide where they fit into your overall educational funding strategy. Advantages of local scholarships Less competition The main advantage of local scholarships is that there is less competition. Since local scholarships are open to a smaller number of students, fewer people will apply, so you will have a statistically higher chance of winning each opportunity you apply to. As a student, you have a lot of responsibilities. Between college applications, keeping up on schoolwork, studying for standardized tests, working a part-time job, and participating in extracurriculars, there’s a lot on your plate. So, it makes sense you’d want each of your scholarship applications to count. Applying to local scholarships can help you earn more scholarship money without spending all your time working on applications. More opportunities for personal appeal If you are an active member of your community, applying for local scholarships is a great idea because it allows you to emphasize your passion for your community. If you are involved in a local organization, or you reference a public place in your neighborhood, there’s a better chance the person reading your application will understand exactly what you mean. This helps create a personal connection and gives you a better chance of a successful application. Disadvantages of local scholarships Lower award amounts The main disadvantage of local scholarships is that they typically offer lower awards than national scholarships. That’s because the community organizations that offer them usually do not have as much funding. However, winning three local scholarships worth $1,000 each is worth more than applying to three high-award national scholarships and not winning any of them! Less prestigious than some national scholarships Some prestigious national scholarships offer students additional benefits, such as networking opportunities and support structures in college. Local scholarships don’t typically offer these benefits, and they usually don’t look as impressive on your resume. That being said, the best strategy for students is to apply for national and local scholarships simultaneously. National scholarships may come with a bigger payoff, but you’re more likely to win a local competition. Remember to cover all your bases While local scholarships are a great opportunity to enter scholarship competitions that have less applicants, they should not be the entirety of your financial aid process. Make sure you take advantage of funding from the Department of Education by filling out the FAFSA. This will gauge your financial need to determine your eligibility for the Pell Grant , federal student loans , and state-wide grants. Checklist for winning local scholarships Look for opportunities through your high school or through community foundations in your area Contact people who have attended college and went to your high school and/or grew up in your neighborhood. These can be family friends, students who have returned to your high school to give talks, and more. Research the history of your community. For local scholarships, it can never hurt to have a comprehensive knowledge of the community you are applying in. Make sure to figure out how you fit into your community, and use this knowledge to stand out in your application essays. Find out if your parents’ employers offer tuition reimbursement opportunities for dependents and immediate family Key Takeaways Local scholarships typically come with lower awards than national scholarships, but they have less competition, so you have a better chance of winning You can find local scholarships through your high school’s guidance counselor and your college’s financial aid office There are many other avenues to explore for local scholarships, including community organizations, your place of worship, and you or your parents’ employer Students should emphasize their commitment to their community in their applications and describe how they will use the scholarship to give back Frequently asked questions How do I find scholarships in my area? The best way to find scholarships in your area is to start with the organizations you’re already involved in. That includes your parents’ employers, your high school, your extracurricular clubs, any sports teams or leadership positions, and your place of worship. Ask your parents to look into the organizations they participate in too. Oftentimes, they may not suspect that the group offers scholarships until they ask. Are local scholarships better? Local scholarships generally have a better chance of success than wide-ranging scholarships since they receive less applicants and are more specialized. However, they also typically offer smaller awards than larger-scale scholarships. So, it’s a good idea to apply for a mix of local and broader scholarships. How can I find scholarships in my local area? The best way to find scholarships in your local area is to talk to your high school’s college counselor and check their website. You can also try community organizations such as 4-H and Scouts. Finally, be sure to try our scholarship search tool for custom-matched local opportunities. Can international students apply for local scholarships? International students can apply for local scholarships from the community they grew up in. They can also try applying for scholarships in the community their college is located in. Oftentimes, colleges also maintain special scholarships for international students. Just make sure that the opportunities you’re applying to do not require applicants to be US Citizens. What are some common mistakes to avoid when applying for local scholarships? The most common mistake you can make when you’re applying for local scholarships is to recycle the application you’re using for national scholarships. Remember – local scholarships are meant specifically to improve the communities they’re offered in. Make sure to tailor your scholarship resume , your personal statement , and your essays to appeal to a sense of community and describe what the place you grew up in means to you.

description: College-specific scholarships In addition to the third-party scholarships listed above, many colleges offer funding for undocumented students. For example, in New York City, CUNY’s Macaulay Honors College offers a full-tuition, laptop, and stipend scholarship for undocumented students who meet their requirements. If you don’t see any programs for undocumented students on your prospective college’s website, it’s always worth calling or emailing the financial aid office. Some schools may have scholarships specifically for undocumented students, while others may have general scholarships that undocumented students are eligible for. Resources for undocumented students Immigrants Rising Immigrants Rising is a California-based organization that increases education access for undocumented students. They release guides on finding affordable tuition, advocate for education policy, and collect scholarships that undocumented students can apply to. While some of their resources are California-centric, they have useful information for students all across the country. The organization also has mental health resources for California-based students. TheDream.Us Also the provider of some of the top scholarships for undocumented students, TheDream.US offers legal resources and links to other sites where DREAMers can find scholarships, programs, and local support. Expert Perspective The FAFSA is not connected in any way to your immigration status. You can fill it out safely regardless of you or your family’s immigration status, and it cannot lead to deportation or any kind of involvement by ICE. title: Types of Scholarships Directory
description: How to craft a scholarship strategy In order to maximize your chances of winning scholarship money, it’s a good idea to come up with a concrete plan for your applications. Here are some tips to get your plan together: Look at a wide variety of scholarship categories Students can qualify for scholarships based on their grades, extracurriculars, demographics, academic interests, and much more. Using the scholarship directory above, as well as our free scholarship matching app , you can find opportunities that match every part of who you are as an applicant. Many students go through the application process without even knowing that certain accomplishments or pieces of their history could qualify them for scholarship funds. Think local Local scholarships are some of the best opportunities for students when paying for college. Since local scholarships are open to a smaller number of students, you’ll have less competition, and a higher chance of winning. Try reaching out to your high school counselor or local leaders, like a Boy Scout leader or someone at your church, to see if your community has a collection of scholarships available. Expert Perspective Some high schools keep their own scholarship database, which can be a great way for students to keep track of scholarships in their area and when they are due. Melody Lipford | Advising Specialist on the Virtual Access Team, College Possible Keep your deadlines straight With scholarships opening and closing all throughout the year, it can be hard to remember when to get your applications in for each one. Making a Google Calendar to keep track of deadlines can be a great idea – you can even program it to email you before the deadline as a reminder. Another great way to keep on top of your deadlines is our free scholarship matching tool , which updates with custom-matched opportunities daily and allows students to store scholarships they are interested in. Treat your scholarship applications like a job or an additional class Another great way to stay on top of your applications is to block off a certain amount of time every week or month to look for scholarships and work on applications. By having this time sectioned off, you’ll be able to keep track of all your deadlines and continue a steady stream of applications. Tips from a Scholarship Winner I treat scholarships no different than I treat schoolwork. You have homework to do every week, and you have scholarships to do every week, based on their deadlines. I like to print out my scholarship applications and put them in different piles. For example, I’ll have an October pile, a November pile, and so on. Joe McGee | Winner of our $10,000 Scholarship, Student at University of Wisconsin-Superior Tips for scholarship applications Research each organization When a scholarship organization chooses a winner, they are looking for someone who aligns with their mission values. So, when you’re answering their prompts, you’re not just trying to answer the question, but also use your answer to demonstrate how you hope to use the scholarship funds to further their mission. Make sure to read up on each organization’s mission and their past accomplishments so that you can make the connection between your future ambitions and those of the organization. Fine-tune your writing Writing about yourself can be challenging, but we have a guide to help you through . We can also help you write a 500 word essay , start your essay , and answer common scholarship essay prompts . Working on this will help you stand out from the crowd of applicants! Get great references Getting strong references , or letters of recommendation, is a great way to stand out to scholarship application reviewers. If a scholarship application requires a letter of recommendation, make sure to ask your recommenders with plenty of time to spare; you’re asking them a favor, so you’re best off if you don’t rush them. What is a scholarship directory? A scholarship directory contains lists of scholarships that students can apply for based on demographics, academics, extracurriculars, or other factors. One of the advantages of browsing scholarship directories is that it can inform you of categories of scholarships you didn’t know existed. Where can I find a list of scholarships? The lists on our scholarship directory are full of scholarships vetted by our team of experts. Most students should browse many different lists of scholarships during their scholarship hunt. This allows you to find opportunities that match all the different categories you may apply for. These can be based on your academic interests, demographics, extracurriculars, and more.

title: Can I Use AI for Scholarship Essays?
description: The use of AI (Artificial Intelligence) is becoming more and more commonplace in today’s world. It has gone beyond the technological sphere and is now being employed in various industries, including retail, entertainment, and even education. While there may be certain benefits to using AI in an educational setting, such as providing students with immediate feedback on assignments or transcribing lectures, issues also arise with AI when students employ it to write or plagiarize essays. Out of the 986 submissions we received for a scholarship we recently, an AI detection tool (GPTZero) found that 410 (42%) of the essays were majorly constructed with AI. But what do we mean by this? Further, how can scholarship providers and applicants alike make sure they’re approaching the new technology in a careful, but practical way? Let’s find out. At a glance As AI becomes more advanced and harder to detect, it’s important for student’s to know the scholarship provider’s policy when it comes to using generative AI for essays. Many scholarship committees are starting to run essays through AI detection software, and if using AI is prohibited, this could lead to applicants becoming automatically disqualified if AI is detected. To avoid potential disqualification, we recommend only ever using AI as a tool to help you format or brainstorm for an essay, but not using it to write an essay for you. What is AI? First, what do we mean by AI? AI, or Artificial Intelligence, is a subfield of computer science that involves building machinery or computers that can reason, learn, and process information in a way that would typically require human intelligence. By “human intelligence,” we refer to skills such as problem-solving, decision-making, or data analysis. This may bring up the question: why is AI necessary at all if it is simply recreating or imitating human behaviors? Good question! This is because, on a large scale, AI is typically able to accomplish these tasks (e.g. analyzing data, applying and calculating formulas, etc.), at a far quicker (near-immediate) pace than humans are capable of. Thus, AI is often used today as a way of bypassing the manual work associated with more routine, formulaic tasks. So, how might this apply to scholarship essays (or essays in general)? Well, essay generation is just one of the many tasks that AI can near-automate. This means that if you were to give an AI tool (such as ChatGPT) an essay prompt and a word count, it can quickly create an essay that answers the question at hand and meets the word count requirement. To give you an idea of what this looks like, let’s give it a try. Example Prompt : Please give me a few sentences about what your perfect day would look like. AI(ChatGPT)-generated answer : “My perfect day would be simple and calm: I’d start by waking up with a clear sense of purpose, then spend the morning exploring new ideas or learning something fascinating. The afternoon would be all about helping people—solving problems, creating things together, or inspiring someone to feel more confident. I’d wrap up the day by reflecting on everything I learned and looking forward to doing it all again tomorrow.” As you can see, the AI produced an answer that answers the question at hand. It addressed what “their” perfect day would involve and what they would do. However, it is also relatively general, not giving any specificity as to what type of “ideas,” “fascinating” information, or “problems” they would discuss. But we’ll explore this more later. For now, let’s look into our own insights from the scholarship we hosted. What percent of essays were AI-generated? As stated earlier, Scholarships360 hosted a scholarship this past summer to which we received nearly 1,000 submissions. The prompt requested that applicants submit a 500-700-word persuasive essay about the benefits of free speech. Ironically, utilizing AI detection software, we found that 42% (410/986) of the responses were found to have a 75% or higher probability of being generated with AI. This rate was determined by a sentence-by-sentence breakdown, which gave each sentence a score based on how it mirrored sentences that had been AI-generated in the past. These scores were then taken altogether to determine an essay’s “overall AI probability score.” This is not to say that AI detectors are fully faultless – schools like Vanderbilt University have even disabled Turnitin’s AI detection tool due to a “1% false positive rate” (Chechitelli, 2023). However, even without the use of the AI detector, we found that we could soon tell which essays had used AI largely based on a combination of the words, phrases, and historical examples used. Our interpretations of whether an essay had been AI-generated or not were, for the most part, fully in line with what the AI detector had spotted. Clear signs essays were AI-generated When it comes to essay generation, AI’s main benefit lies in its efficiency. Students may feel tempted to use it solely by the amount of time they will save by not having to write an essay at all. With this said, it is important to remember that AI is essentially following a formula. Anyone who feeds it the same prompt and word count requirement is likely to get a very similar response, forgoing the personalization found in self-written essays. While reading through the 986 responses, it became abundantly clear that there were certain words and phrases that AI seemed to favor. Here is a list of a few of those we saw repeated time and time again throughout the submissions, and how often we saw them: Common AI-generated words/phrases/trends (with frequency) : “Cornerstone” Present in 62% of essays with a >75% AI probability rate Present in 6% of essays with a <75% AI probability ate “Bedrock” Present in 20% of essays with a >75% AI probability rate Present in 1% of essays with a <75% AI probability ate Starting with “Dear _” Present in 20% of essays with a >75% AI probability rate This trend may be because the prompt requested that essays be written as a “letter or essay” Present in 5% of essays with a <75% AI probability rate Many variations of essays beginning with “In our/In the/In _” with unusually decorative language Examples: “In the vibrant tapestry of human society” “In the annals of human history…” Risks to using AI for scholarship essays Similarities in word use As seen above, perhaps the clearest disadvantage of using AI to generate a scholarship essay is its limited range of word choices. Students who employ AI to write their essays run the risk of their essays quickly being pegged as AI-generated, and thus, out of the running for a scholarship award. This is not to say that one word out of the 200, 500, or even 1,000 in your scholarship essay will make or break you. However, the repeated usage of unusual words (e.g. “cornerstone”) seen in many other essays may be a red flag to scholarship committees. Similarities in arguments and examples The similarities between our AI-generated submissions did not stop at just word choice, but extended into the arguments used and historical examples applicants cited. Of our nearly 1,000 scholarship essays reviewed detailing why free speech is a preferable policy, hundreds of them cited these same points: (1) that a lack of free speech would “hinder societal and technological progress” and (2) that free speech allows for “open dialogue” and “open-mindedness.” On their own, these arguments are not bad at all. They are valid reasons why one would prefer having free speech in a society. With that said, many of these claims were then followed by the same or very similar historical examples. Some of the most common historical references cited among the submissions included: Nazi Germany, North Korea, the Soviet Union, China, or the U.S. Civil Rights Movement. Even now, when I asked ChatGPT for “historical examples to persuade me that free speech is better than its alternative,” I received four out of these five same answers (except North Korea). This is what the main problem with AI essay generation boils down to: similarity and a lack of originality. Possible inaccuracies in information On the topic of historical examples, it is important to remember that many AI tools have only periodically updates. Thus, we recommend double-checking the accuracy of any historical claims before using them in an essay. This is especially true for more modern events, as the information is more likely to have been updated in the recent months or years. Lack of originality/individuality The bottom line when applying for scholarships is that you are often facing hundreds, if not thousands, of competitors. If the words, arguments, or themes of your essay are very common amongst the cohort you’re applying with, you are likely not helping your chances of winning a scholarship. Whether it be a great argument, flowing prose, or an interesting anecdote, scholarship committees are ultimately looking for something that will pique their interest in a sea of submissions. An essay to remember… Scholarships360 CEO & Cofounder Will Geiger still remembers a girl from Kentucky who wrote her essay about her drive home from school. He recalls that you felt like you were along for that car ride as she observed her town, the things that she saw from the car, the people in her community, etc.. The essay was effective because the student shared her unique perspective and showed the reader what her drive home was like. This is the type of essay that only this unique student could have written, and it showed. Unfortunately, however, such an authentic voice is exactly what AI-generated essays are devoid of due to the formulaic nature of Artificial Intelligence. Thus, taking time to personalize your essay and making it true to your own experiences will likely be more than worth the effort. Keeping this in mind, it raises the question of how scholarship providers and applicants alike should approach scholarship applications in the modern day. More specifically, what are some things scholarship providers can look out for when reviewing submissions, and how can applicants effectively use AI to help write scholarship essays without facing potential disqualification? Let’s take a look. Navigating AI essays as a scholarship provider In the past three years, I have reviewed nearly 10,000 scholarship essays submitted for a variety of scholarships, each with unique prompts and word counts. Approximately half of these were reviewed before the widespread launch and use of AI tools like ChatGPT, and roughly half have been reviewed since. Despite this, I had never before seen a batch of essay submissions in which so many mimicked one another until this year. As AI continually grows in its capabilities, it feels unlikely that its influence will decrease anytime soon. So, how can scholarship providers navigate this new landscape of AI-generated submissions? 1. Keep an eye out for commonalities between essays As you read through submissions, monitor for any unusual patterns. This could include the frequent use of words, phrases, or claims (across essays) that you otherwise don’t see often. These could all point to an AI generated essay. 2. Create unique essay prompts Try to craft essay prompts that require applicants to rely upon or detail examples from their own lives or experiences. Such anecdotes are difficult for AI to recreate and should lead to more genuine, human responses. 3. Require additional project or application materials Rather than relying solely on essays to review applicants, scholarship providers might also require the submission of other creative or project-based content (e.g. videos, art, portfolios). Such materials are typically harder to fabricate than essays. 4. Incorporate interviews Requiring an interview portion allows scholarship providers to speak to applicants and ask them about their essays directly. Applicants can be asked to elaborate on certain points in their essay and dive deeper into their reasonings. Such interviews can be conducted after finalists are chosen. The submission of short videos is another way to verify authenticity. 5. Make it clear you’ll be assessing for AI usage Another option is to forewarn applicants that AI usage (via an AI detector or other processes) will be utilized in scoring. Ideally, this should prevent applicants from attempting to use AI as they know it will be a detriment to their score. However, providers should bear in mind that it may also inspire applicants to try and “disguise” their AI usage, making it harder to detect. How can I effectively use AI to help me write a scholarship essay? While we do not recommend using AI to write or generate an entire essay, don’t write if off entirely as a tool. Here are just a few ways that students can use AI to their benefit: 1. Brainstorming AI can be a useful tool to brainstorm ideas for your essay. To avoid potentially using an overused idea or argument, it may be helpful to ask the AI tool for questions that prompt deeper reflection on your part. From there, you can use your personal experiences or anecdotes you’ve thought of to support your argument. For example, let’s take a look at some very common scholarship prompts and how you could ask an AI tool to give you your own questions to consider when formulating an answer: Scholarship prompt: “Why do you deserve this scholarship?” Question for AI: “What are questions students should consider when they’re thinking of why they deserve a scholarship?” Scholarship prompt: “Tell us about a time when you’ve overcome a challenge and what you learned from the experience.” Question for AI: “What are questions students should consider when answering the question: “Tell us about a time when you’ve overcome a challenge and what you learned from the experience.”” Scholarship prompt: “What are your academic or professional goals? How will earning this scholarship help you achieve them?” Question for AI: “What are questions students should consider when answering the question: “What are your academic or professional goals? How will earning this scholarship help you achieve them?”” Pretty simple, right? In response to all these questions, your AI tool of choice should return a list of many, more specific questions to help you conceptualize an answer and even outline your own essay based on your own experiences. 2. Proofreading grammar Once your essay is complete, running it through an AI tool may be helpful. AI can be a tool for detecting any grammar issues that may be present. This way, you can avoid making small mistakes while ensuring that the content of the essay is still yours. 3. Checking for clarity Beyond grammar, AI tools can also be useful to check or improve the clarity or readability of your essay. After completing your essay, asking an AI tool to summarize the content for you can help ensure that your point is getting across smoothly. Final thoughts And that’s it! We have now covered many of the advantages and disadvantages of using AI to write or review scholarship essays. Whether you’re the one submitting or reading them, we wish you much success navigating this new technological landscape. Remember, Scholarships360 offers nearly every resource to help you write your best scholarship essays. Learn how to write winning scholarship essays , including how to start a scholarship essay and how to end a scholarship essay as well. Learn how to confidently write a 250 word essay and a 500 word essay , and even an essay about yourself ! Happy writing!

Worth $25,000 Scholarships for undergrads by grade level Whether you are a college freshman or a transfer student, we have specific guides to help you find and apply for scholarships: Scholarships for High School Freshman Scholarships for High School Sophomores Scholarships for High School Juniors Scholarships for High School Seniors College Freshmen Community College Students College Sophomores College Juniors Transfer Students College Seniors How to win undergrad scholarships Here are a few tips for finding and winning scholarships and financial aid for an undergraduate education. Apply for need-based financial aid Your first step should be to apply for need-based aid, including Pell Grants , Federal SEOG Grants , and work study . These are strictly based on your need, so your academic standing should not impact them as long as you are making Satisfactory Academic Progress . The two major financial aid applications are the FAFSA and the CSS Profile . These applications serve to assess your financial need. Schools have their own deadlines for each application, so make sure that you get everything in on time! Apply to many scholarships to increase your odds of winning A key part of any good scholarship strategy is applying to a broad array of scholarship opportunities. The more you apply to, the more chances you have of winning! Scholarships can take many forms, such as video scholarships , local opportunities , and scholarships based on your major or your background . Check your college’s financial aid office or high school counseling office for scholarships Your college’s financial aid office or your high school’s counseling office should be your first stop for college scholarships since they may be able to offer other forms of aid as well (like grants or work study programs). If you are not currently on campus, you can consult their website and reach out to a representative via email. Look for departmental scholarships Many colleges, such as the University of South Carolina , offer scholarships to current students on a departmental basis. Students who show particular promise in one field of study may be eligible to receive funding from their department for their additional years of schooling. You can try consulting your professors, your advisor, or the chair of the department you’re majoring in to see what opportunities are out there. Study abroad scholarships If you plan on studying abroad, you may be eligible for scholarships! There are many places to look for study abroad scholarships. These include your school’s study abroad department, the organization running the program you’re enrolling in, and our very own list of scholarships for students who are studying abroad ! As studying abroad can often end up being expensive for students, it’s a good idea to pursue these options to reduce your costs. Frequently asked questions about undergraduate scholarships How do I find scholarships that no one applies for? One of the best ways to find scholarships with little competition is to apply for local scholarships or scholarships with niche requirements. For example, scholarships reserved for students in your town, people of your religious background, or people in your specific academic field will have far less applicants. It’s a good idea to seek out scholarships that are as specific to your situation as possible. The fewer applicants, the better chance you have of winning! Is the Sallie Mae $2000 scholarship legit? Yes, the Sallie Mae $2000 scholarship is awarded every month to a student. However, it’s a good idea to apply to other scholarships in conjunction with Sallie Mae, in order to increase your chances of funding your education. What is the most prestigious undergraduate scholarship? While there is no one most prestigious undergraduate scholarship, the Presidential Scholarship is definitely in the running. Only 161 students receive the scholarship every year. Full Ride scholarships also tend to be some of the most prestigious, and hey, having all your educational expenses paid for doesn’t sound too bad either!

title: The Florida Benacquisto Scholarship: Everything You Need to Know
description: Want to learn more about the Florida Benacquisto Scholarship Program? Well, you landed in the right place! If you are an upcoming Florida high school graduate who is also recognized as a National Merit Scholar, keep reading to learn more about the incredibly generous Benacquisto Scholarship and how to qualify! What is the Benacquisto Scholarship? The Benacquisto Scholarship is a merit based scholarship for Florida high school graduates who receive National Merit Scholar recognition. Students who are eligible receive an award equal to the cost of attendance for their eligible Florida institution. What are the eligibility requirements for the Benacquisto Scholarship? Below is a list of the eligibility requirements for the Benacquisto Scholarship: Earn a standard Florida high school diploma Be a National Merit Scholar Enroll in an eligible Florida postsecondary institution during the fall academic term following high school graduation Be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen Enroll full-time in a baccalaureate degree program What is a National Merit Scholar? A National Merit scholar is a scholarship competition in which there are roughly 7,000 winners out of the 3,500,000+ students who take the PSAT each year. A National Merit finalist becomes a scholar by receiving one of the following: National Merit $2,500 scholarship Corporate-sponsored merit scholarship College-sponsored merit scholarship National merit scholarship The one-time $2,500 scholarship is open to all students regardless of financial need or college choice. College-sponsored national merit scholarship Students who are National Merit finalists will nominate a college or university as their first choice in order to receive funding from that particular institution. Corporate-sponsored merit scholarship Many corporations will offer awards for children of their employees, residents of locations where the company operates or for Finalists who have career interests aligned with the corporation. Related: How to win a National Merit scholarship What is the award amount for the Benacquisto Scholarship? The award amount for the Benacquisto Scholarship is the total estimated cost to attend college full-time and may include the cost of tuition and fees, on-campus room and board , supplies , books , travel, and miscellaneous expenses. What is the application process like for the Benacquisto Scholarship? There is no separate application for the Benacquisto Scholarship. Rather, eligible students are identified through their National Merit Scholar status and must ensure their college has their National Merit Finalist information. How do you renew the Benacquisto Scholarship? You do not need to submit an application in order to renew the Benacquisto Scholarship. Rather, your renewal will be determined at the end of the second semester. You will automatically be renewed for the Benacquisto Scholarship if you have earned credit for all hours enrolled and earned a minimum GPA of 3.0 . If you fail to meet these renewal requirements, then you will become ineligible to continue in the program. Frequently asked questions about the Benacquisto Scholarship What colleges offer the Benacquisto Scholarship? Here is a list of Florida colleges and universities that offer the Benacquisto Scholarship: Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University Florida Atlantic University Florida International University Florida State University New College of Florida University of Central Florida University of Florida University of Miami University of South Florida Can out-of-state students receive the Benacquisto Scholarship? Unfortunately no. The Benacquisto Scholarship is reserved for Florida residents only. However, there are plenty of other scholarships out there perfect for out-of-state students ! Be sure to browse our website to find the best scholarships for your particular situation! How long is the Benacquisto Scholarship awarded for? The scholarship is awarded for up to eight semesters or 4 years of undergraduate study as long as you maintain eligibility to stay in the program. Can I transfer schools and still receive the Benacquisto Scholarship? Yes, students who want to transfer can switch the scholarship to another eligible Florida institution. However, you must notify the new institution and ensure all eligibility requirements are met in order to continue to receive the Benacquisto Scholarship.

title: California College Promise Grant: What It Is and How to Apply
description: California can be an expensive state for students in terms of cost of living and tuition. However, if you are a California resident you could be eligible for the California College Promise Grant that allows you to attend community college in California for free! Keep reading to learn more about the California College Promise Grant! What is the California College Promise Grant? The California College Promise Grant allows eligible California residents to have community college enrollment fees waived including tuition. However, you will still have to pay for textbooks and the cost of fees such as parking fees and health fees. Also see: Top California scholarships Who is eligible for the California College Promise Grant? In order to be eligible for the California College Promise Grant you will need to meet the following criteria: Lived in California for at least one year as a resident or AB 540 eligible student Demonstrate financial need on the FAFSA Meet academic standards by maintaining a GPA of 2.0 or higher and completing more than 50% of your coursework What schools qualify for the California College Promise Grant? Most California community colleges ! Be sure to double check with your community college’s particular rules for enrollment in order to ensure they offer the program and that you qualify for the California College Promise Grant. Related: Top reasons to attend a community college How do I apply for the California College Promise Grant? In order to apply for the California College Promise Grant you must complete the following steps: Submit the FAFSA or CADAA Submit your community college application at CCCApply.org It is important to note that the application opens during the summer semester of each academic year and must be completed every year. The application itself is quite simple (especially in comparison to the FAFSA application!). It is a two-page application in which you provide information about yourself and your parents if you are a dependent student . What about the remaining fees I need to pay? The California College Promise Grant only covers tuition and certain fees. Therefore, you may be wondering about how to pay for the other expenses such as books or room and board . Luckily, a lot of community colleges in the California area offer their own promise grants in addition which can cover those types of expenses. For example, some colleges will offer book vouchers, counseling services and priority class registration in addition to free tuition. The application process for the school-specific promise grants varies based on the specific school. Therefore, be sure to research schools you are interested in to find out eligibility criteria as well as how to enroll in these programs. Also see: Which states offer tuition-free community college? Start your scholarship search Vetted scholarships custom-matched to your profile Access exclusive scholarships only available to Scholarships360 members Get Started Frequently asked questions about the California College Promise Grant Do I have to pay back the California College Promise Grant? No! You do not have to pay back the California College Promise Grant at all. However, if you do not maintain your eligibility you can lose the grant. Do I only need to apply once? You will need to reapply for the California College Promise Grant every academic year by submitting a new FAFSA. How long can I receive the California College Promise Grant? You can receive the California College Promise Grant for an unlimited number of semesters as long as you meet the academic standards set by your particular community college.

title: Top 54 Trade School Scholarships in August 2026
description: 📝Sample Essay from a Scholarship Winner Here's a winning scholarship essay from Chloe L, who won our "Follow Your Own Path" Essay Scholarship , which is a great option for community college students. Read the essay below and I'll offer some commentary on what made this a winner. Prompt: How is your current education supporting your career goals? Essay I have always loved nature. It has been a passion of mine since I was a little girl. As I got older, I became more aware and developed the critical thinking skills to see everything we were doing to the world around us, from the little things like littering to things as big as deforestation. And ever since then, I have always known I had to do something to protect the beautiful environment that surrounds us. In middle school I fell in love with my biology class and my teacher helped me to realize that science was my favorite subject. That year I figured out that science was how I was going to contribute to conservation efforts. At Colorado State University I am majoring in the degree of zoology. This degree most closely aligns with my goals. This program will allow me to develop a specialized set of skills geared towards ecosystems, conservation, and biodiversity. Ensuring I have the knowledge I need to truly protect and care for these creatures as well as their homes properly. My bachelors degree at Colorado State could be the one thing that would finally allow me to make the type and size of impact I truly desire to have and to change this world for the better. I am taking classes such as Calculus, Chemistry, Biology, and so many others. This is giving me the basis of everything I need to be successful in this field! Why it worked Chloe uses her essay to describe exactly what motivates her to pursue her educational track. Then she gets into specifics. She describes the classes she's taking and her major and the skills she's trying to develop. This shows she's put a lot of thought into her educational track, and she has a plan. We are left confident that Chloe would make the most out of these educational funds. Will Geiger Scholarships360 Co-Founder, Former Admissions Officer

title: Top 16 Poetry Scholarships in August 2026
description: Top 3 poetry scholarships overall We choose our poetry scholarships by identifying reliable organizations that provide significant rewards and have a long history of offering their scholarships. U.S. Creative Writing Awards Scholarship – Open to college-bound high school seniors who create and submit an original piece of written fiction, drama, poetry, a memoir/personal essay, or a spoken word piece. How to win poetry scholarships Hone your writing skills When it comes to the work you submit for these scholarships, make sure you are choosing your strongest work. It may be a good idea to get opinions from teachers or mentors about your work. Tailor your work to the prompt Check to see whether or not the scholarship you’re applying to has a prompt, and if it does make sure to tailor your work to fit it! Read our application tips Once you’ve picked out some poetry scholarships to apply to, it’s time to get to it! Crafting creative and compelling pieces of poetry application can take time, but we’ll help you when it comes to any other supplemental materials in your application. title: Skechers Foundation Scholarship Program
description: The Skechers Foundation provides $300,000 in scholarships to support 60 high-achieving high school seniors. This scholarship program comprises four individual scholarship programs: SKECHERS Financial Hardship Scholarship SKECHERS Academic Excellence Scholarship SKECHERS Promising Leaders Scholarship SKECHERS Athletic Performance Scholarship Who is eligible to apply for the Skechers Scholarships? To be eligible for the Skechers Scholarships, students must be high school seniors who have a minimum GPA of 3.0. Students also must be planning on attending a two- or four-year accredited college/university, technical, or vocational education program. Additionally, three of the scholarships have additional eligibility requirements: The SKECHERS Athletic Performance Scholarship is only open to students who are playing a sport at the collegiate level. The SKECHERS Financial Hardship Scholarship requires students to have demonstrated financial need. The SKECHERS Promising Leaders Scholarship is open to students who have a track record of leadership in their school or community. How do I apply for the Skechers Scholarships? Students can apply to each of the scholarships directly with their Scholarships360 profile. Each application will include 1-2 essay questions and short answers that students will need to complete. Each scholarship application will also include an “additional information” section where students can share any circumstances that may have impacted their high school experience. This is optional but gives students the opportunity to share extra information with the scholarship committee. When is the scholarship deadline? The deadline for the scholarships is April 15, 2026 at 11:59 pm EST. How are scholarship winners selected? The scholarship committee will be considering a variety of criteria, including academic performance, essay responses, and financial need when selecting scholarship recipients. How will the scholarship be disbursed to students? All scholarship checks will be sent directly to the students’ college or university financial aid office. Can students apply to multiple Skechers Scholarships? Yes, assuming a student is eligible, students are able to apply to all four Skechers Scholarships. However, students may only receive one scholarship. When are Skechers scholarships awarded? The winners of the Skechers scholarships will be announced by May 22, 2026. Can international students apply for Skechers scholarships? Only U.S. Citizens can apply for the Skechers scholarships. What documents do I need to apply for the Skechers scholarships? To apply for the Skechers Scholarships, students will need to attach a copy of their most recent transcript (this can be an unofficial transcript that ideally includes grades from senior year) and their high school profile. A high school profile provides additional information about your school’s curriculum. In most cases your high school’s guidance counselor should be able to provide this short document, but in some cases (e.g. homeschooled students) you might need to work with teachers/counselors to put one together. Check out this helpful resource with a sample high school profile . Should I fill out the optional personal statement? The optional personal statement on the Skechers scholarships is for students to explain extenuating circumstances that may have affected their high school performance. You should fill out this statement if you experienced some kind of hardship that affected your high school performance. Examples of this could include: Providing childcare for a sibling Working to help support your family Illness in the immediate family Being diagnosed with a learning disability Health problems What if I have questions about these scholarships? If you have questions about these scholarships, please reach out to scholarships@scholarships360.org.
